correctness.rationale: Normalized disk monomial moments are 1/(n+1). Taking the squared A² norm of P² gives the fourth moment; its sole phase-sensitive term comes from |b²+2ac|² and demands aligned phases at an interior optimum. When c=0 the quotient is 1+2v−5v²/3 for v=|b|²/(2||P||²_A²), attaining 8/5 at v=3/5. For c≠0 take u=|a|/|c| and q=3|b|²/(2|c|²). The q derivative has affine numerator with positive intercept and strictly negative slope for all u≥0, so it has a unique global maximum in q>0. After substitution the derivative of the remaining rational quotient has sign opposite to 30u³+35u²−5u−4; its unique positive root gives a strict maximum above both u=0 and the c=0 face. Independent exact differentiation and elimination reproduce q*=(3/2)u*(3u*+1) and the constant polynomial (the resultant multiplier is 2618387280). The quotient at u=1/3 is 2791/1042>13/5, and the constant polynomial is strictly increasing above 13/5, isolating the largest root. Magnitude and phase equality give exactly the stated scalar-and-rotation family; |a/c|=u*, whereas a/c=u* only in the aligned real representative. The invariant b²/(ac)=3u*+1>2 differs from 4/3 for every nonconstant K₂; K₂ at the origin is constant, and K₁ with |w|²=3/4 attains the degree-one maximum.

value.rationale: Area A² normalization makes the fourth-moment quotient a natural exact measure of concentration among finite polynomial profiles, and reproducing kernels are the natural point-concentration candidates. Degree two is the first degree permitting a genuine relative phase in this moment problem. The exact optimizer family resolves whether the degree-one kernel prescription survives that new interaction, and gives a sharp benchmark for finite Bergman concentration rather than a numerical comparison at an arbitrary weight.
residual_risks: No pattern for higher polynomial degrees, other exponents, or the unrestricted same-weight inclusion is established.
